fieldValues.title: srs-rust#1015's premise about JsonStore was stale — it was retired in #783 Phase 4
fieldValues.summary: #1015 (and its parent #813) assumed a separate JsonStore struct still exists with a real batch-rollback override, distinct from FileStore's no-op default. Ground-truth reading of the current srs-rust codebase (commit da38854, 2026-09-09) shows JsonStore was retired in #783 Phase 4: there is no json_store.rs file, and the store_conformance.rs test helper init_json_store() actually returns a FileStore (opened via a .srsj session). MemoryStore also uses the RepositoryStore trait's no-op batch defaults — it never had real rollback either, contrary to the implicit assumption that only FileStore lacked it.
evidence: grep for "impl RepositoryStore for" in crates/srs-repository/src found exactly three implementors: FileStore, MemoryStore, and a BrokenManifestStore test double — no JsonStore

migrate_identity_service.rs already carries its own comment (pre-dating this unit): "No store implements in-memory rollback since JsonStore's retirement (srs-rust#813) — what protects a .srsj document is the projection boundary, and that only helps if the whole operation fails as one."
the store_conformance.rs test file's own #[ignore] reason on the old batch_abort_rolls_back test already said the same thing before this unit touched it
fieldValues.body: A future unit reasoning about the batch seam, JsonStore, or #813/#1015's scope should start from this ground truth rather than the issue text's premise: there are exactly two store implementors today (FileStore, MemoryStore), neither has ever supported real rollback, and the actual safety net for .srsj/session-backed operations is the projection boundary (flush-only-on-success), which is independent of RepositoryStore's batch seam entirely.
